name: No! No! hair remover

card.summary: A handheld device by Radiancy that uses a heated wire (Thermicon) to remove hair at home, marketed for gradual reduction of hair growth on legs, body and face.
card.note: Manufacturer claims come from the company; an independent study was small.

quick.overview:
The no!no! is a handheld hair removal device from Radiancy that heats a thin wire in a probe. Radiancy's account, reported by Dermatology Times, is that the heat reaches the follicle and crystallizes the hair shaft to stop regrowth. People use it to reduce the need to shave or wax on legs, bikini area and face.

A 2007 study in the Journal of Drugs in Dermatology tested it on 12 completers and reported median leg hair clearance of 48% right after the treatment series and 43.5% at 12 weeks, with lower results on the bikini area. The company claims hair growth reduces by up to 64%.
quick.how: Users pass the probe over the skin in a regimen the company describes as twice a week for 12 weeks, then once every one to two weeks. The device is marketed as painless, and treatment is done at home without a clinic.
quick.risks: The product uses heat on the skin, and heating devices can cause irritation or burns if misused, so manufacturer instructions apply. The published study reported that safety was evaluated, though its available text does not detail specific adverse events. Independent data are limited to that small study.

lead: The no!no! is a handheld thermal hair removal device made by Radiancy. Radiancy describes its Thermicon technology as heating the hair follicle to crystallize the hair shaft and stop it growing back, using hot blades that contain a thermal wire.[1] People use it at home to cut down on shaving or waxing on the legs, bikini area and sometimes the face.

In a 2007 clinical evaluation published in the Journal of Drugs in Dermatology, James M. Spencer tested the no!no! Thermicon on the lower legs and the umbilicus-bikini area. Twenty subjects were enrolled and 12 were treated and evaluated. Median hair clearance on the legs was 48% post-treatment and 43.5% at 12 weeks, and on the bikini area 15% at 12 weeks. The author concluded that efficacy and safety on the legs appeared comparable to those of laser devices.[2]
The company's claim, reported by Dermatology Times in 2008, is that the device reduces hair growth by up to 64%, and it is marketed as painless. That figure comes from the manufacturer.[1]

chain: Heated wire passed over the skin surface
Heat reaches the hair shaft and follicle
Less visible hair and less frequent shaving
angle.text: The device removes hair by heating it at the skin, and users treat repeatedly to reduce regrowth, aiming for smoother skin with fewer shaving sessions. The reported leg results varied with body area.

infobox: Twice weekly for 12 weeks, then every one to two weeks [1]
Up to 64% reduction in hair growth [1]

paras: According to the manufacturer, the device heats the hair follicle and crystallizes the hair shaft, with hot blades containing a thermal wire intended to damage the follicle.[1] It is a heat-based contact device rather than a laser targeting pigment.

The 2007 Journal of Drugs in Dermatology study had subjects perform 6 supervised and 6 unsupervised self-treatments, twice weekly for 6 weeks, with follow-up visits at 2, 6 and 12 weeks after the last treatment. Hair counts were compared before treatment, after treatment and at follow-up. Median clearance was 48% post-treatment and 43.5% at 12 weeks for the legs, versus 15% at 12 weeks for the umbilicus-bikini area. The study was small, with 20 enrolled and 12 evaluated.[2]
The product is promoted for self-treatment at home. Dermatology Times reported the company's regimen and its painless-treatment claim in 2008, noting the figures came from Radiancy.[1]

timeline.event: Spencer publishes a clinical evaluation of the no!no! Thermicon in the Journal of Drugs in Dermatology.[2]
Dermatology Times reports the company's claim of up to 64% reduction in hair growth.[1]
